summary: At segment 0 step 168, the Caveman quest transition should load dat/Cav-fila.lua. js/mklev.js computes Cav-fila but its loader registry has no entry, so it falls through to ordinary room generation and consumes the below-Medusa rn2(5) draw. C instead enters mkmaze.c:makemaz and sp_lev.c:load_special; loading the complete Lua program first runs nhlib.lua's already-implemented alignment shuffle (rn2(3)). Port and register the whole Cav-fila.lua program.

source.branch: The Caveman reaches a Home quest filler level above the locate level; mklev.c:makelevel selects Cav-fila.lua and special-level loading runs the nhlib initialization before the program body.
callers: mklev.c:makelevel selects the role filler name Cav-fila.lua
mkmaze.c:makemaz and sp_lev.c:load_special execute the selected level program
js/mklev.js:generate_level computes Cav-fila; SPECIAL_LEVEL_LOADERS lacks it, so the C caller path is skipped
dependencies: nhlib.lua alignment shuffle (already implemented in js/mklev.js and js/nhlua.js)
sp_lev.c level-generation API and existing js/quest_levels.js loader helpers

evidence: The admitted v62 manifest sourcePointers identify mklev.c:makelevel1275-1285 -> mkmaze.c:makemaz -> sp_lev.c:load_special -> nhlib.lua initialization -> Cav-fila.lua.

The whole upstream dat/Cav-fila.lua program (lines 6-35) sets a solid-fill base, applies mazelevel/noflip flags, initializes mines-style terrain with walls, then creates up/down stairs, seven random objects, four random traps, five hostile bugbears, one hostile h-class monster, and one hostile hill giant.

js/mklev.js:760-772 checks SPECIAL_LEVEL_LOADERS[fillName] before calling makemaz; js/mklev.js:1795-1820 builds the registry from QUEST_LEVEL_LOADERS, which currently has no Cav-fila entry. The ordinary fallback then consumes rn2(5) at js/mklev.js:1295, matching the JavaScript side of the first divergent call.

Fresh post-publication scan at commit aa0cdbbacca08c9fc000bb87cfd982931db46e07 stops matching at segment 0 step 168: C consumes rn2(3)=0 in nhlib.lua shuffle(), while JS consumes rn2(5)=2 in the ordinary below-Medusa check. The recorded boundary screen has a wall-versus-floor mismatch at row 2, column 60.
The saved v62 evaluation at ef4963eb5ba2f7992cc8c6d92bd1ace9fb796678 records 168 of 197 screens matched; the fresh scan confirms the same source owner after the latest publication.
